newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil federal deficit narrows in Jan-Feb period.
newsitem.headline: Brazil federal deficit narrows in Jan-Feb period.

text.p: The Brazilian federal government and the Central Bank posted an operational budget deficit in January and February equivalent to 2.28 percent of gross domestic product, a senior Finance Ministry official said.

Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic policy secretary, said the result was a significant improvement over the 2.73 percent of GDP operational deficit posted by the federal government and the Central Bank in the same period last year.
"This fiscal result underscores a clear improvement in the fiscal area," Mendonca de Barros told reporters as he presented a monthly report on the economy drawn up by the ministry.
In February, the federal government reported a 799 million real surplus in its primary result, which unlike the operational result does not include debt servicing costs.
In January, the federal government posted a primary deficit of 1.24 billion reais.
In its report, the ministry said February's improvement "began the process of adjustment which foresees a primary surplus of 1.5 percent of GDP" in 1997.
